macro.text: Meta announces a $95 billion stock offering to fund its AI expansion.
Neocloud stocks fall after Elon Musk says more than 200 of them face "guppy-level death".
Trump says he will soon decide whether to "make a deal" with Iran or "finish it off".
Verizon lifts its annual forecasts and signs a more than $2 billion AI infrastructure deal with AWS.
Goldman cuts its Kospi forecast by 25%, a read-through for the global AI trade.
Oil slides over 2% as traders weigh Saudi attack risks and demand destruction.

briefs.read: The tone is mixed with a mild risk-on lean in tech: QQQ is up about 0.7% premarket while SPY is roughly flat, the VIX closed Friday a little lower near 19, and WTI is down about 2% to around $101, though the 10-year yield is slightly higher near 4.99%. There are no high-impact scheduled releases today, so the day has no single data event; the main items are company and headline driven, chiefly how the market takes Meta's $95 billion stock offering and the pressure on neocloud and AI infrastructure names. Iran is the open geopolitical risk, with Trump saying a decision on a deal or further action is coming soon, and any headline there could move oil and the indexes quickly. Before taking a setup, it is worth waiting for the first 15-minute range to form and seeing whether QQQ's premarket strength holds once Meta and the AI names trade at the open.
